question: What is the main goal of workplace safety and health in nursing?

options.A: Protecting workers from work-related injuries and illnesses
options.B: Providing free medical treatment for community members
options.C: Ensuring maximum financial profit for the institution
options.D: Reducing the number of working hours for staff

explanation: You can't pour from an empty cup! Keeping yourself safe and healthy on the ward is the number one priority so you can care for others safely. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why do nurses and healthcare workers face unique safety risks on the job?

options.A: They face constant exposure to infectious agents and physical strain
options.B: They are completely immune to common hospital-acquired infections
options.C: They rarely interact with patients who have contagious diseases
options.D: They spend most of their working hours sitting at a desk

explanation: From lifting patients to handling needles and dealing with infections daily, nursing is physically demanding. Knowing this helps you protect yourself early! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h1)

question: In safety management, what is considered the MOST effective way to deal with a hazard?
explanation: If you completely remove the danger, nobody can get hurt by it! That makes elimination the ultimate win in safety. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h2)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) ranked at the very bottom of safety controls?

options.A: It relies heavily on human behavior and fails if not worn correctly
options.B: It completely removes the hazard from the work environment
options.C: It is the only method approved by hospital management
options.D: It is always more expensive than engineering controls

explanation: PPE is just a barrier—if you forget to put it on properly or take it off carelessly, you are still exposed. That's why it's our last line of defense, not the first! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is a great example of an engineering control in a hospital?

options.B: Wearing a heavy-duty apron during surgical procedures
options.C: A training session on proper handwashing techniques
options.D: A policy stating that needles must never be recapped

explanation: Engineering controls use physical design or equipment to protect you automatically, like needles that shield themselves so you don't accidentally prick your finger. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h3)

question: A clinic manager limits the number of continuous hours a nurse works in a high-radiation department. What type of control is this?
explanation: When management changes work schedules, policies, or rules to limit your exposure time, they are using administrative controls. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h3)

question: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) rank when we talk about safety controls?

options.A: As the last line of defense

explanation: Gloves, masks, and aprons are crucial, but they are our final backup when other safety measures like equipment design or policies aren't enough on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h4)

question: Why is taking off (doffing) your PPE safely such a big deal for nurses?

options.A: To comply with clothing fashion standards in the hospital
options.B: To speed up the process of leaving an isolation room
options.C: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused by another staff member
options.D: To prevent self-contamination from pathogens resting on the outer surface

explanation: The outside of your gown and gloves is covered in germs! If you take them off clumsily, you'll accidentally spread those germs right onto your skin or scrubs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h4)

question: What is the main focus of ergonomics in nursing?

options.A: Ensuring patients walk unassisted as early as possible
options.B: Increasing the speed at which nurses can complete patient admissions
options.C: Reducing the financial cost of hospital bed purchases
options.D: Adapting tasks and equipment to fit the physical capabilities of the worker

explanation: Ergonomics is all about working smarter, not harder—adjusting your environment and tools so your body doesn't take unnecessary strain. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h5)

question: You need to help move a heavy patient up in bed. Which of these follows safe ergonomic practices?

options.A: Holding the patient far away from the body to keep uniform clean
options.B: Bending sharply at the waist with straight knees to gain momentum
options.C: Twisting the torso quickly while lifting to reach the bedside table
options.D: Using a mechanical lift or asking a colleague for assistance

explanation: Never try to be a lone hero with heavy lifting! Always ask a colleague to team-lift or use mechanical aids to protect your lower back. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h5)

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day

explanation: Good old handwashing (or using an alcohol rub) is your superpower. It stops germs dead in their tracks before they reach you or your next patient. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h6)

question: Why do hospitals require standard precautions for every single patient, no matter their diagnosis?

options.A: Infectious diseases only spread after a laboratory confirms them
options.B: It saves time so nurses do not have to check patient charts
options.C: Patients prefer knowing their care involves extra safety steps
options.D: Any patient's blood or body fluid can carry hidden infectious pathogens

explanation: You can't always tell who has an infection by looking at them. Treating every body fluid as potentially infectious keeps you safe every time. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h6)

question: What is the main reason hospitals conduct pre-employment health checks for new nursing staff?

options.A: To establish a baseline health status and ensure fitness for the job
options.B: To lower the hospital's monthly utility and supply expenses
options.C: To test the worker's knowledge of medical terminology
options.D: To guarantee that the worker will never contract a disease at work

explanation: Checking your health before you start helps the hospital know you're fit for the ward's demands and gives a clear record of your health baseline. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h7)

question: Why are routine screenings, like annual tuberculosis tests, so important for hospital staff?

options.A: They completely prevent bacteria from entering the hospital building
options.B: They catch potential occupational infections early before symptoms worsen
options.C: They replace the need for wearing masks during patient care
options.D: They test the patient population for chronic illnesses

explanation: Routine checks help catch any sneaky occupational exposures early on, meaning you can get treated quickly and stay healthy! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h7)
